author: rinn
body:
Hey!

As you already know, many of the Senior Staff Departments have been working to improve all aspects of the staff team that fall under their sector. Recently, there have been forms such as Senior Staff feedback, TeamSpeak feedback, etc. The Department of Feedback and Staff Consistency has created a document that will allow the community to give all of their feedback on each and every moderator individually, based on their performance on the server and forums. Use this link to begin giving out feedback. Please do not make false or joke responses, and I would suggest that your responses for each Moderator be two sentences or longer. Good luck! :)

Regards,
The Department of Feedback and Staff Consistency

EDIT: Yes, I understand there is an additional thread, however issues have occurred with the response spreadsheet and an updated form was created.

EDIT #2: I've removed all required questions since most of you probably won't have feedback for all moderators.

replies.author: rinn
replies.body:
This form was requested, as the moderators would like to get as many opinions on their work as possible. We, as the senior staff, are responsible for making sure that the moderators are doing work efficiently. However, why should we be more entitled to giving feedback than the community? After all, it isn't the senior staff whom the moderators work hard for, as much as you may deny it. It is none other than the community, so I feel that the community itself should be able to express how they feel about the staff team, and instead of flaming on the forums, a feedback survey has been created to organize and send out legitimate responses to moderators. In the case of a member making, to use your words, "cowardly swipes," the unnecessary or extremely rude comments are deleted from the response sheet and are therefore considered illegitimate. However, if a community member wishes to speak directly to a moderator about their efficiency, Skype and TeamSpeak are always available for those who do not mind revealing themselves.

EDIT: In reply to your second post, this feedback form is not to address issues that we cannot find. It is simply to give moderators a different perspective of their current abilities since most feedback relayed to them was by other staff members.

replies.author: Howsie
replies.body:
Ok, so now you're telling me that the moderators are not confident in their abilities? As much as I would like to respect your honesty, the constant scrounging for approval via surveys and 'am i gud mod' threads is just the sign of a fractured and weak team. 

The other thing I'd like to reiterate - it is not the responsibility of non-staff members to dictate how the team conduct themselves. That should be done via a cohesively written, public post in a centralised area of the forum. This is important for two reasons. One - Transparency among all members of the community.  Two - The issue becomes open for discussion. Leading to heavy critiquing and better ideas forming from initial ideas.

replies.author: Myworld6
replies.body:
You do make valid points. However, I personally see these threads as an opportunity for community members to give their feedback on the staff and what they believe the staff team need to do.

I respect your reasons, and I'm grateful that you voiced them. It's nice to see more people who are willing to provide valid, rational arguments for why they are against an action that is taken by the staff team.

I also agree with your point about a constant feedback system. This is a system that is sorely needed. It could benefit the staff team by providing us with a source of constructive criticism, and the community by providing them with a way to communicate with the staff team.

I do not speak for the staff team on this matter. I speak about my own personal opinion on the matter.
